statements.impact_statement: Netty codec vulnerability fixed in 4.1.133.Final / 4.2.13.Final. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run any network server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections. There is no inbound socket for an attacker to exploit.

statements.status_notes: Netty: [Bzip2Decoder] Infinite Loop in RLE State Machine Leads to Event-Loop Thread Hang. The Bzip2Decoder handler in Netty's compression codec pipeline is vulnerable to a denial-of-service attack through a malformed bzip2 stream that permanently captures the event-loop thread in an infinite loop, in the run-length encoding (RLE) state machine within Bzip2BlockDecompressor.read().
statements.impact_statement: Netty Bzip2Decoder infinite loop in the RLE state machine on a malformed bzip2 stream, hanging the event-loop thread. Liquibase dependency management includes Netty versions below the fixed 4.1.136.Final release (pom.xml:124, commercial-databases/liquibase-cassandra/pom.xml:49), so this assessment does not rely on a version-fixed claim. Bzip2Decoder is an opt-in compression codec that must be explicitly added to a Netty pipeline; none of Liquibase's Netty consumers (Cassandra driver via netty-codec, or the Azure/AWS/MongoDB HTTP transports) configure bzip2 compression. A focused grep for Bzip2Decoder, Bzip2Encoder, and io.netty.handler.codec.compression.Bzip2 across Java and XML sources returned zero hits.
